reaction.episode: CORRECTION through Oct 30: SPX $7,580.07, down 3.37% from its 120-day high, 1.52% below its 50-day but 3.7% above its 200-day. SMH $522.49 is between zones, down 22.23% from its high and 0.58% above its 200-day; NVDA $204.64 occupies Zone 1. VIX is 19.42 with no rollover, HY OAS is 3.26 and calm, and the mechanical capitulation tally is 2 of 4. Data is fresh, not stale.
reaction.invalidation: A SPX close below its 200-day at $7,309.76 combined with HY OAS above 4%, or SMH closing below the Zone 2 floor at $470 with credit cracking, proves the Watch stance wrong — the episode is no longer a correction and the ladder is void.

ladder.response: Tranche A probe: deploy 25% of new money per the deployment ladder — staged buys, not a full position
ladder.trigger: SMH prints Zone 2 ($470-505) and/or NVDA prints Zone 2 ($175-185), with the mechanical tally at 3 of 4 or better

ladder.response: Treat as the trap case: no chasing, no adds; the failed retest confirms the correction continues and Zone 2 stays the target
ladder.trigger: Bounce into the failure zone: SMH $580-600 or SPX $7,750-7,820, then rejection on a closing basis

ladder.response: Stand down: the correction becomes a regime break, the ladder is void, and all deployment pauses pending a re-audit
ladder.trigger: HY OAS above 4% or VIX sustained above 25, or SPX closes below its 200-day at $7,309.76

ladder.response: Confirmed-bottom condition met: Tranche C (50%) becomes eligible on the re-entry read, sized per the ladder
ladder.trigger: Failed first bounce followed by a second low that holds, with the 10-year falling — or a held close above SPX $7,750-7,820 / SMH $580-600

ladder.response: Wait — no probe on a single-name break; Zone 2 on SMH is the index-level confirmation the ladder requires
ladder.trigger: NVDA breaks below the Zone 1 floor at $200 while SMH stays above Zone 2

reaction.trapRisk: The pivot-and-fail scenario is the live risk: a sharp bounce into SMH $580-600 / SPX $7,750-7,820 on a clean midterm or jobs outcome would look like a bottom but is the failure zone. Entries change accordingly — no chasing the first bounce, no adds until the failure-zone retest delivers its verdict or Zone 2 prints with the tally at 3 of 4.

strategyPosture: Watch. The correction is active but unconfirmed as a bottom: NVDA is in Zone 1, yet the mechanical tally is only 2 of 4, with no volume-climax reversal and no VIX rollover. New money stays in bills; no adds until Zone 2 prints or a confirmed reversal forms.

themes.counterRead: The rollover narrative has run ahead of the credit data: nothing in lending standards or spreads confirms a broad break. But the divergence itself is real — if credit flips, rotation becomes rollover fast, so the gap is the thing to track, not dismiss.
themes.dataAnchor: SPY is only 3.3% below its 52-week high while the Mag7 average sits 16% below theirs — a 12.7-point divergence gap. Bank lending standards are LOOSE (SLOOS 0%, far below the ~40% stress threshold) and HY OAS is 3.26, calm. The index is holding while leadership rotates, not breaking.
themes.label: Mag7 unwind: rotation, not rollover
themes.narrative: The tape reads as a broad market rollover: QQQ fell 3.16% on the day and is down 6.64% over one month, with GOOGL 31.5% below its 52-week high and META 15.4% lower over the month.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS breaking above 4% or SLOOS tightening toward 40% would convert this from rotation to rollover.

themes.counterRead: Multiple compression can persist long after fundamentals diverge from price — NVDA sits in Zone 1 ($200-210) but SMH is between zones and neither has printed a floor. The setup is real, but the entry is not yet earned: Zone 2 (SMH $470-505, NVDA $175-185) plus a capitulation tally of 3 or better is the trigger, not the drawdown alone.
themes.dataAnchor: Revenues are still growing through the drawdown: NVDA +61.4% YoY at $204.64 (RSI 35.1), AVGO +55% YoY with a 42.1% FCF margin at $326.08, 34.1% below its high, LRCX +131.3% YoY at 45.5% below its high, and AMAT +11.4% YoY at 47.3% below its high. The dislocation list counts 34 names, most of them sentiment-driven rather than earnings-driven.
themes.label: AI infrastructure: fundamentals ahead of price
themes.narrative: The AI trade is broken — a financing trade unwinding, with SMH down 22.23% from its 120-day high and 17.14% over 20 days, and NVDA down 15.91% from its high.
themes.watchFor: SMH printing Zone 2 ($470-505) with the mechanical tally reaching 3 of 4, or a volume-climax reversal with VIX rolling over.

themes.counterRead: Oversold is not a bottom. The price action and the missing confirmation signals agree: this is a real unwind, not a washout that has finished. Buying the first bounce here is buying into the failure zone, not into a floor.
themes.dataAnchor: The damage matches the leverage: CONL -19.51% today, COIN -9.55% today and -23.27% over the month, BMNR -7.02% today and -24.65% over the month, RDDT 65.2% below its 52-week high with RSI 17.5, GOOGL RSI 21.4. Oversold readings are extreme across the board, yet the mechanical tally confirms only 2 of 4 signals — no volume-climax reversal and no VIX rollover.
themes.label: Leveraged and crypto-adjacent blowout
themes.narrative: Capitulation is underway in the leveraged complex — TQQQ fell 9.49% on the day and is down 20.37% over the month, CONL is down 44.16% over the month, and RDDT collapsed 28.86% in a single session.
themes.watchFor: A VIX rollover from its 5-day high of 19.42, or SMH volume climax with an intraday reversal (close in the upper half of the range).

themes.counterRead: The bond rally is fear-driven, not dovish-Fed-driven, so the rate relief is fragile. As long as spreads stay contained, the equity drawdown reads as multiple compression and rotation — if HY OAS breaks 4%, the regime changes and the ladder stands down.
themes.dataAnchor: The curve is positively sloped (2s10s +0.37), the real 10-year is 2.64%, and HY OAS is 3.26 with credit marked calm and not cracking. The 10-year has now printed five straight closes under the 5.2% line. Rates are high, but the funding channel is open.
themes.label: Credit and rates calm while equities stress
themes.narrative: Higher-for-longer is pressuring multiples — the FOMC decision of Oct 27-28 is still the active high-signal event, with headlines running on Fed signals for higher rates, and the 10-year sits at 4.98% with the 2-year at 4.61%.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS above 4% or a 10-year close back above 5.2% would break the calm-credit read.

themes.counterRead: Positioning is cautious but not panicked, which cuts both ways: a clean event outcome can fuel a sharp bounce straight into the failure zone (SPX $7,750-7,820, SMH $580-600), while a bad one has room to push SMH into Zone 2. Either way the week resolves the range.
themes.dataAnchor: VIX is 19.42, up 12.91% on the day and at its 5-day high, but that is a modest level for an event week — no spike-and-rollover pattern, and the VIX spike-rollover signal is unconfirmed. SPX is down only 3.37% from its 120-day high and still 3.7% above its 200-day average of 7,309.76.
themes.label: Event-week overhang: midterms and jobs
themes.narrative: The market is waiting: the US midterm elections (Nov 3) and the October jobs report (Nov 6) are both live watch events, with headlines framing the week as a sell-off colliding with earnings and the election.
themes.watchFor: SPX closing above $7,750-7,820 (failure-zone retest) or below its 200-day at $7,309.76 after the Nov 3 and Nov 6 prints.

whereWaveBuilds: The next move most likely materializes as either a push down into Zone 2 (SMH $470-505, NVDA $175-185) if selling continues through the midterm and jobs prints, or a sharp bounce into the failure zone (SMH $580-600, SPX $7,750-7,820) that fails on retest.
